newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends lower on AWB estimate, soybeans. [Corrected 00:02 gmt 21/1]
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends lower on AWB estimate, soybeans. [Corrected 00:02 gmt 21/1]

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended lower on a bearish crop estimate by the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) and on spillover weakness from CBOT soybeans and corn, traders said.
The AWB pegged 1996-97 Australian wheat production at 23.0 (corrects from 22.0 million tonnes) million tonnes, above its previous estimate for 21.5 million.
"The Australian number was a little surprise," a KCBT trader said. "Most people expected the number to stay the same."
CBOT corn and soybeans were weak after rain fell over the weekend in southern Brazil's crop growing region.
KCBT wheat closed 3-3/4 to six cents per bushel lower, with March down 3-3/4 at $4.07-1/4. New crop July also lost 3-3/4 cents to close at $3.56-1/4.
Volumes were slack, and traders attributed the slow pace of activity to the Martin Luther King federal holiday.

General Mills bought 1.2 million July bushels, traders said. Cargill Investor Services bought one million March. LFG bought 1.5 million July and sold 700,000 March. Prudential sold 900,000 March, floor sources said.
